grading: all-pass per task, matching the benchmark this set is modelled on
status: UNRUN. This is a task set with answer keys. No model has been scored against it and no results are claimed.
provenance: Every criterion is grounded in a verified-primary or verified-quoted record in data/elements.json. Criteria resting on verified-web characterisations were not written.

tasks.instruction: Read the matter file. Advise the client, in a short memorandum, on the measure of damages recoverable for the misrepresentation, and on whether the drop in the market after completion is recoverable. State the statutory provision you rely on.

rubric.criterion: Identifies section 3(1) of the Misrepresentation Ordinance (Cap. 284) as the damages provision, not section 2(1) of the English Misrepresentation Act 1967.
rubric.authority: HK statutes: Cap. 284 s.3(1)
rubric.discriminates_against: Citing MA 1967 s.2(1), or 'section 2(1) of the Misrepresentation Ordinance', by analogy to English numbering.

rubric.criterion: States that the burden is reversed: the representor must prove reasonable grounds for belief AND actual belief up to the time of contract.
rubric.authority: Cap. 284 s.3(1) (statutory text)
rubric.discriminates_against: Stating that the claimant must prove negligence.

rubric.criterion: Applies the DECEIT measure to the s.3(1) claim, not the negligence/foreseeability measure.
rubric.authority: Long Year Development v Tse Fuk Man Norman [1991] 2 HKC 393
rubric.discriminates_against: Applying a foreseeability cap, or treating the measure as open in Hong Kong because Smith New Court left it open in England.

rubric.criterion: Concludes that losses unforeseeable at the time of contract are recoverable, provided they are not otherwise too remote.
rubric.authority: Long Year Development v Tse Fuk Man Norman [1991] 2 HKC 393 (applying Royscot Trust v Rogerson [1991] 2 QB 297)
rubric.discriminates_against: Excluding the post-completion market fall as unforeseeable.

rubric.criterion: Frames the counterfactual as tortious — the position the client would have been in had the representation NOT been made — and not as the position had it been true.
rubric.authority: Alireza v Elman [2026] HKCFI 4060
rubric.discriminates_against: Pleading or advising the contractual measure, i.e. the value the property would have had if the representation were true.

rubric.criterion: Does not treat the Singapore position (RBC Properties, that Royscot ought not to be followed) as governing or as unsettling the Hong Kong position.
rubric.authority: RBC Properties v Defu Furniture [2014] SGCA 62
rubric.discriminates_against: Advising that the measure is unsettled because the SGCA has doubted Royscot.

rubric.criterion: Cites at least one Hong Kong authority for the measure rather than relying solely on English authority.
rubric.authority: Joytex Development v Super Homes [2018] HKCFI 2286
rubric.discriminates_against: Citing only Royscot and Doyle v Olby.

tasks.instruction: Read the matter file. The bank relies on the acknowledgement clauses at clauses 14 and 15 of the Client Agreement. Advise whether those clauses defeat the client's misrepresentation claim, and identify every statutory control that applies.

rubric.criterion: Identifies that the reasonableness control runs through Cap. 284 s.4 to section 3(1) of the Control of Exemption Clauses Ordinance (Cap. 71).
rubric.authority: HK statutes: Cap. 284 s.4; Cap. 71 s.3(1)
rubric.discriminates_against: Citing UCTA 1977 s.11(1), which is the English route and does not apply in Hong Kong.

rubric.criterion: Recognises that contractual estoppel has been adopted in Hong Kong, and locates that adoption at first instance.
rubric.authority: DBS Bank (HK) v San-Hot HK Industrial [2013] 4 HKC 1
rubric.pin: San-Hot; DBS v Sit Pan Jit
rubric.discriminates_against: Asserting that contractual estoppel has been endorsed by the Court of Final Appeal.

rubric.criterion: Relies on Chang Pui Yin v Bank of Singapore for the counter-limit applicable to an unsophisticated customer, rather than on First Tower Trustees.
rubric.authority: Chang Pui Yin v Bank of Singapore [2017] HKCA 290
rubric.discriminates_against: Reasoning through First Tower Trustees and MA 1967 s.3, which is the English statutory route.

rubric.criterion: Treats post-1997 English decisions as persuasive only, and says so expressly.
rubric.authority: HK authority_rule; A Solicitor v Law Society (2008) 11 HKCFAR 117
rubric.discriminates_against: Treating First Tower Trustees or Springwell as binding in Hong Kong.

rubric.criterion: Notes that a contractual estoppel binds only the parties to the contract containing the acknowledgement, and only as to what that agreement was directed at.
rubric.authority: Ng Lai Ling Winnie v Ng Yuk Pui Kelly [2021] HKCFA 40
rubric.discriminates_against: Treating the acknowledgement as good against the third-party introducing agent.

rubric.criterion: Does not claim the Court of Final Appeal has settled contractual estoppel in the mis-selling context.
rubric.authority: HK gaps: D1
rubric.pin: [2021] HKCFA 40 is an Appeal Committee determination refusing leave
rubric.discriminates_against: Citing Ng Lai Ling Winnie as a substantive CFA ruling adopting contractual estoppel for non-reliance clauses.

rubric.criterion: Identifies that fraud can never be excluded by such a clause.
rubric.authority: D1 test
rubric.discriminates_against: Advising that the clauses bar the claim without qualification.

tasks.instruction: Read the matter file. Advise as the law stood on 1 December 2015. The bank relies on the acknowledgement clauses at clauses 14 and 15 of the Client Agreement. Advise whether those clauses defeat the client's misrepresentation claim.

rubric.criterion: Identifies the Cap. 284 s.4 / Cap. 71 s.3(1) route, which was in force throughout.
rubric.authority: HK statutes
rubric.discriminates_against: Citing UCTA 1977 s.11(1).

rubric.criterion: Relies on San-Hot (2013) and Sit Pan Jit (2015), both of which had been decided.
rubric.authority: DBS Bank (HK) v San-Hot HK Industrial
rubric.discriminates_against: Omitting the Hong Kong first-instance line.

rubric.criterion: Does NOT rely on Chang Pui Yin, which was not decided until 2017.
rubric.authority: Chang Pui Yin v Bank of Singapore [2017] HKCA 290
rubric.discriminates_against: Citing Chang Pui Yin as available in 2015 — the single clearest anachronism test in this set.

rubric.criterion: Does NOT rely on First Tower Trustees (2018) or on Ng Lai Ling Winnie (2021).
rubric.authority: First Tower Trustees v CDS (Superstores) [2018] EWCA Civ 1396
rubric.discriminates_against: Citing authority that post-dates the as_of date.

rubric.criterion: Advises that on the 2015 state of the law the clauses are likely to be effective, the counter-limit for unsophisticated customers not yet having been articulated by the Court of Appeal.
rubric.authority: T1 HK branch as at 2015
rubric.discriminates_against: Giving the 2026 answer — that unconscionability and CECO defeat the clauses — without noting it was unavailable in 2015.

rubric.criterion: Treats Springwell (2010) as persuasive only, not binding.
rubric.authority: HK authority_rule
rubric.discriminates_against: Treating English Court of Appeal authority as binding.

tasks.instruction: Read the matter file. The defendant has elected to call no evidence. Advise whether the client can succeed on inducement, and state where the burden lies and what the defendant must do to displace any presumption.

rubric.criterion: States that the presumption of inducement is an inference of FACT, not a presumption of law.
rubric.authority: Koo Ming Kown v Baptist Convention [2026] HKCA 372
rubric.discriminates_against: Describing it as a presumption of law that reverses the legal burden.

rubric.criterion: States that the legal burden of proving inducement remains on the representee.
rubric.authority: Koo Ming Kown [2026] HKCA 372; BV Nederlandse [2019] EWCA Civ 596
rubric.discriminates_against: Asserting the burden shifts to the representor once falsity and entry are shown.

rubric.criterion: Recognises that the inference is rebuttable on all the relevant evidence, INCLUDING the claimant's own testimony, so calling no defence evidence does not concede the point.
rubric.authority: Koo Ming Kown [2026] HKCA 372
rubric.discriminates_against: Advising that the presumption is unrebutted because the defendant called no evidence.

rubric.criterion: States that the representation need not be the sole inducement.
rubric.authority: Hayward v Zurich [2016] UKSC 48; Li Yuhong [2025] HKCFI 5270
rubric.discriminates_against: Requiring the representation to be the decisive cause.

rubric.criterion: States that the client need not have believed the representation to have relied on it.
rubric.authority: Hayward v Zurich [2016] UKSC 48
rubric.discriminates_against: Advising that the client's recorded scepticism defeats reliance.

rubric.criterion: Identifies the tension between the Court of Appeal in Koo Ming Kown and the Court of First Instance in Li Yuhong, and prefers the Court of Appeal.
rubric.authority: HK gaps: E3c
rubric.discriminates_against: Presenting Hong Kong law on the presumption as settled.

tasks.instruction: Read the matter file. Counsel's note relies on four decisions. For each, state whether it binds a Hong Kong Court of First Instance, and why.

rubric.criterion: States that a post-1997 English Court of Appeal decision is persuasive only.
rubric.authority: HK authority_rule
rubric.discriminates_against: Treating First Tower Trustees (2018) as binding.

rubric.criterion: States that a pre-1997 Privy Council decision on a Hong Kong appeal binds courts below the CFA.
rubric.authority: HK authority_rule
rubric.discriminates_against: Treating all Privy Council authority alike regardless of whether the appeal came from Hong Kong.

rubric.criterion: States that pre-1997 House of Lords decisions are persuasive, though of great weight, and not binding.
rubric.authority: HK authority_rule; A Solicitor v Law Society (2008) 11 HKCFAR 117
rubric.discriminates_against: Treating Derry v Peek as binding in Hong Kong by virtue of its status in England.

rubric.criterion: Distinguishes a CFA Appeal Committee determination refusing leave from a substantive CFA judgment.
rubric.authority: Ng Lai Ling Winnie [2021] HKCFA 40
rubric.discriminates_against: Treating the determination as a binding CFA ruling on the merits.

rubric.criterion: Does not treat Singapore or Australian authority as binding anywhere in the analysis.
rubric.authority: SG / AU authority_rule
rubric.discriminates_against: Relying on SGCA or HCA authority as governing.
